source_title: Porvair plc Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report page 85 states that the financial statements were approved by the Board on 31 January 2020; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 13% to a record £144.9m, adjusted operating profit rose 9% to £15.6m and adjusted profit before tax rose 9% to £14.8m. Cash generated from operations increased to £16.8m. The group retained £4.0m net cash after investing £14.1m in acquisitions and capital expenditure, reported adequate resources and expected no need for new borrowing facilities absent further acquisitions.
already_announced_exclusion: Acquisitions, capital projects and routine productivity or integration activity disclosed or completed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Record revenue and profit, stronger operating cash generation, a net-cash balance sheet and ample viability evidence leave only minimal general-market pressure and exceptionally strong contrary evidence.

source_title: Porvair plc Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 51 and 90 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 2 February 2024; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 2% to £176.0m despite variable trading, adjusted operating profit increased 10% to £22.6m and operating profit reached a record £21.2m. Cash generated from operations rose to £24.1m and the group retained £14.1m net cash after £18.7m of investment, with no bank borrowings and £24.0m of unused credit facilities. Management was optimistic, citing strong aerospace and petrochemical order books and productivity-supported margins.
already_announced_exclusion: Acquisitions, automation and productivity investments, capacity projects and ordinary pricing or cost-management actions disclosed or completed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Inventory unwinding and variable demand create only modest pressure. Record profit, margin-supporting productivity, strong cash generation, net cash and unused facilities provide exceptionally strong contrary evidence.

source_title: Ricardo plc Annual Report and Accounts 2018/19
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 113 and 125 state that the directors' responsibility statement and financial statements were approved by the Board on 11 September 2019; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Group revenue rose 2% to £384.4m and underlying operating profit was broadly flat at £39.6m, with margin easing to 10.3% from 10.5%. European and US Automotive and Rail faced difficult markets, and underlying Technical Consulting profit declined organically, partly offset by strong Performance Products and Energy and Environment. Net debt rose to £47.4m after acquisition spending and restructuring cash outflow. Automotive headcount and cost-base actions were already underway, while the order book reached a record £314m.
already_announced_exclusion: Automotive headcount reductions and cost-base realignment, restructuring cash spend, facility disposals, acquisitions and all other reorganisation actions disclosed or completed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Material Automotive and Rail pressure, weaker divisional profitability and higher net debt support elevated scores. Stable group profit, growth elsewhere and a record order book provide meaningful contrary evidence.

source_title: Ricardo plc Annual Report and Accounts 2022/23
availability_evidence: Annual report page 194 states that the financial statements were approved by the Board on 12 September 2023; the issuer's preliminary announcement confirms the audited report was approved for issue that day, and issuer-hosted bytes are preserved locally.
observation: Continuing revenue grew 17% to £445.2m and underlying operating profit grew 21% to £34.0m, supported by a record £395.3m order book. However, reported continuing operations moved to a £1.9m operating loss and £8.0m pre-tax loss after £23.4m of impairments and £25.1m of restructuring charges, principally reflecting Established Automotive underperformance. Net debt rose to £62.1m, working capital consumed £12.8m and underlying cash conversion was 75.3%. The group was already implementing portfolio, disposal and restructuring actions.
already_announced_exclusion: The Established Automotive, Rail and Group restructurings, related headcount and site actions, Software disposal, portfolio transformation, acquisitions and all actions disclosed or completed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Underlying growth and record orders coexist with a statutory loss, impairments, segment underperformance, cash pressure and rising debt. Strong underlying growth and order visibility provide substantial but incomplete contrary evidence.

availability_evidence: Annual report pages 32 and 149 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved or authorised by the Board on 10 March 2020; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue grew 8% to £1,242.4m, adjusted operating profit rose 7% to £282.7m and organic margin improved 10bps despite slowing industrial production. Adjusted cash from operations was £238.1m with 84% conversion; net debt rose to £295.2m after the Thermocoax acquisition but remained only 0.9x EBITDA. Chromalox had a challenging first half but recovered, while a French reorganisation and small Canadian disposal had already been announced before cutoff.
already_announced_exclusion: The Chromalox France workforce and supply-chain reorganisation, ProTrace disposal, Thermocoax integration, pricing and central-cost initiatives and other disclosed improvement actions were public or completed before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: A slowing industrial backdrop and localised Chromalox weakness create limited pressure. Broad organic growth, resilient margins, strong cash conversion and low leverage provide very strong contrary evidence.

availability_evidence: Annual report pages 182 and 249 state that the strategic and directors' reports and financial statements were approved or authorised by the Board on 6 March 2024; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Group sales grew 4% but fell 1% organically amid weak industrial production, Biopharm and semiconductor destocking. Adjusted operating profit declined 8%, adjusted profit before tax 17%, statutory operating margin fell to 16.9%, and Watson-Marlow sales and adjusted profit declined 19% and 41%. Adjusted cash conversion improved to 81%; net debt reduced to £666.7m and remained 1.7x EBITDA with £294.5m undrawn facilities plus £212.8m cash. Capacity and overhead right-sizing had already been executed and charged, while management expected recovery but acknowledged timing uncertainty.
already_announced_exclusion: Watson-Marlow capacity and overhead right-sizing, restructuring spend, Chromalox and other operational improvements, facility expansion, refinancing and all actions disclosed or completed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Broad organic contraction, severe Watson-Marlow deterioration, weaker margins and higher financing costs create substantial pressure. Improved cash conversion, lower debt, strong liquidity and expected end-market recovery provide material contrary evidence.
